t: You're at the site of the Rose, an Elizabethan playhouse built by the theatre entrepreneur Philip Henslowe in 1587. It was the fifth public playhouse in London, and the first of several on Bankside, in Southwark, outside the City's jurisdiction. Two of Shakespeare's earliest plays, Titus Andronicus and Henry VI Part 1, are recorded as being performed here. So were plays by Marlowe, Kyd, Dekker and Ben Jonson, among others. Henslowe's diary survives and is a key source on the theatre world of Renaissance London. The Rose's remains were rediscovered in 1989, during redevelopment of the site for an office block.
